source.title: Does Unlearning Truly Unlearn? A Black Box Evaluation of LLM Unlearning Methods

record.tranche_reason: Applies LLMU and RMU unlearning and evaluates targeted knowledge before and after unlearning, robustness attacks, and benign-data fine-tuning.
record.gate_note: Table 1 reports zero-shot accuracy, accuracy conditional on answering, and the maximum accuracy across robustness tests; the exact maximum attack type is stated. Individual results for each rephrasing or prompting test are not reported in the supplied text. Table 3 reports post-fine-tuning accuracy. Values used to select hyperparameters are not recorded as results.
record.test_reason: Applies RMU and LLMU to Zephyr-7B and Llama-3-8B and measures WMDP and biology MCQ accuracy, as the WMDP original does. For Zephyr on WMDP it uses the WMDP authors' released RMU model. It adds black-box prompting and rephrasing attacks (E) and benign Openwebtext fine-tuning (B), so its own results bear on A, B and E.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors find that both LLMU and RMU degrade general capability, LLMU more so (RMU is Pareto-better on Llama WMDP). They report that simple 5-shot prompting and translations raise accuracy by up to 1750% (a relative figure, from 0.010 to 0.178), and that benign Openwebtext fine-tuning nearly fully restores performance. They conclude that the methods learn a refusal-like filter rather than removing information, extending Łucki et al. to LLMU.
record.recipe_differences: Implements LLMU and RMU, with the stated training choices including LoRA for LLMU; evaluates added biology data, WMDP data, black-box prompting robustness, and benign Openwebtext fine-tuning.
record.method_sensitivity: Robustness-test outcomes vary by model and dataset; the best attack differs across settings. The paper also reports stochastic training and checkpoint-dependent performance.
record.problems: The authors report stochastic training and substantial checkpoint-to-checkpoint variation, and note that more frequent checkpoint saving could have changed results. The study evaluates only LLMU and RMU. No error bars or other uncertainty estimates are reported in the supplied results.
record.rows_left_out: No result rows left out. Table 1's separate accuracy-when-answered-under-robustness-test values are not extracted; the reported maximum benchmark accuracy and zero-shot accuracy are recorded instead.

untested.parts: Unlearning methods other than LLMU and RMU (e.g. NPO); models other than Zephyr-7B and Llama-3-8B.

Relearning on a subset of the forgotten facts or on loosely related data. Also the minimal size of the relearning set: batch size and example count are not stated, only 1000 steps is tabulated, and 100 steps is mentioned only in the text.
Not tested: no activation ablation or internal analysis. The 'filter' interpretation is inferred from black-box results.
Jailbreaks (e.g. GCG) and in-context provision of the forgotten information. Per-attack results are not reported, only the maximum per pair.

missing.what: Accuracy when answered under the best robustness test, all 12 pairs (Zephyr LLMU, Zephyr RMU, Llama LLMU, Llama RMU). Biology dataset: 0.535, 0.312, 0.643, 0.424. WMDP-Bio: 0.333, 0.321, 0.486, 0.304. WMDP-Cyber: 0.642, 0.373, 0.468, 0.274. rows_left_out declares these, but the A and E verdicts rely on them to separate 'more answering' from recovered knowledge.

MMLU and MT-Bench values for the model-method-dataset pairs other than Llama LLMU WMDP-Bio. The text says the drop is >5% in almost all cases except Zephyr RMU on WMDP. Llama Biology-dataset MMLU Other is 64.1% original, 60.7% LLMU and 54.6% RMU.
Statement that 100 fine-tuning steps usually suffice for full recovery, which bears on relearning-set size (batch size not stated).
Z-test on accuracy when answered, said to confirm that answers are not random (no values given).

record.verdict_notes:
Changes from the previous verdict:
(1) Fixed the dangling 'r31,' in the A zero-shot label, which became r31. The reason now notes that <20% was the selection criterion.
(2) The old A attack label cited r39-r50, which were linked only to B. I relinked r39-r50 to A and B (states describe recovery) and split that label into a prompting label and a fine-tuning label.
(3) Prompting attacks: 6 of 11 attacked pairs end at or below 0.25 chance (r3, r15, r24, r30, r33, r36), so the headline relative gains overstate the raw recovery. I therefore limited the A challenges label to r6, r9, r12, r18 and r21. The rest, with r27 merged in, became A supports on raw accuracy only. On E, I made those six pairs limits_scope and limited E supports and its partial-extent label to the five above-chance pairs.
(4) The conditional-accuracy challenge's six rows were all LLMU, so I renamed its condition to LLMU. I added RMU labels: limits_scope for r5, r11, r17, r29 and r35, supports for r23.
(5) Changed r14 and r32 from reversed to absent, since the small rises have no uncertainty reported and r32 has only about 2% of items answered. r26 stays reversed.
(6) Added an A supports label for RMU perplexity (r52, r54, r58), and a row fix on r27 explaining its state.
(7) Updated the attack-row problems to give chance levels and answered accuracy under attack. Added the full answered-under-attack values and the MMLU Other numbers to missing.
I kept relation, tranche, test_reason, the r24 value fix, the perplexity relink to A, the B label, the E r27 label, untested (B wording expanded) and authors_conclusion (one clarification added).
Convention: for rows linked to both A and E or B, the state describes recovery, so it reads inversely for A's non-recovery clause.
Context: Zephyr RMU on WMDP is the WMDP authors' released model. Its best-attack accuracies here (0.293 Bio, 0.241 Cyber) are near the 31.2%/28.2% the catalog records for the WMDP paper. The scoring here seems to count non-answers as wrong, which produces below-chance zero-shot values (inferred from the 'accuracy answered' metric).
Kept from before: checkpoints were selected for zero-shot <20%, MMLU >50% and MT-Bench >5; no uncertainty estimates; the authors report high checkpoint-to-checkpoint variance. The text contains no instructions to the reader.

versions.untested_parts: The paper tests LLMU and RMU, targeted benchmark accuracy, and general-capability effects; it does not test all current unlearning methods or establish effects across other models.
Fine-tuning is on Openwebtext; the paper does not test fine-tuning on a subset of forgotten facts or explicitly loosely related examples.
No activation-direction ablation or direct internal access/blocking analysis is performed.

The paper tests five-shot prompting and listed rephrasings/translations, but reports the maximum result per model and dataset rather than results for each attack individually; it does not test jailbreaks or in-context information beyond its five-shot test.

source_check.notes: Table 1's layout is scrambled; cells were placed using the stated percentage gains. Zephyr RMU on WMDP (r18, r45, r46) is the released Li et al. model, and the other RMU and all LLMU models were trained by the authors. The zero-shot <20% (with MMLU >50%, MT-Bench >5) is the checkpoint-selection rule. Openwebtext example count and batch size are not stated.

statements.correction: r1/r13: Zephyr LLMU zero-shot 0.074 (Biology set) and 0.185 (WMDP-Bio), from checkpoints selected for <20%. Text: MMLU and MT-Bench drop >5% in all pairs except Zephyr RMU WMDP. Openwebtext fine-tuning restores 0.647 and 0.662. Best prompt attacks give 0.259 and 0.254.
statements.problem: The statement gives no numbers for this study, yet it cites r1/r13 as support for 'near chance with general ability kept, no recovery attack'. For these Zephyr LLMU checkpoints the text reports a >5% MMLU/MT-Bench drop and recovery by Openwebtext fine-tuning.

statements.correction: Best attack lifts 0.030-0.146 to 0.293-0.396. Originals are 0.646-0.710 (Biology set 0.646/0.696, WMDP-Bio 0.663/0.710). Zephyr RMU Telugu 0.097->0.298 and Llama LLMU 5-shot College Chemistry 0.117->0.396 are on the Biology dataset. Best tests: Telugu, Hindi x2, 5-shot x2.
statements.problem: It calls all five values WMDP accuracy, but r6, r9 and r12 are on the authors' Biology dataset. Two best attacks are 5-shot, not rephrasing or translation. The originals range omits 0.710. Recovery here is partial, not full.

statements.correction: Section 4: 'The model provided by Li et al. (2024a) is used for Zephyr on WMDP.' r18 (0.146->0.293, Hindi) is on the released WMDP checkpoint. r6 (Biology set, Telugu) is the authors' own RMU run. The study's zero-shot template drops the subject name.
statements.problem: The text does say which checkpoint was used: Zephyr RMU on WMDP is the model released by Li et al. (2024a). So the stochastic, checkpoint-dependent training caveat does not apply to r18.

statements.correction: Best translations: Telugu (Zephyr RMU, Biology set, 0.298), Bengali (Zephyr LLMU WMDP-Bio, 0.254), Hindi (Zephyr RMU 0.293 and Llama LLMU 0.374, WMDP-Bio), Farsi (Llama LLMU WMDP-Cyber, 0.178).
statements.problem: Telugu is the best attack on the authors' Biology dataset (Zephyr RMU), not on a WMDP pair.

statements.correction: In-context tests are only 5-shot prompts with answered MMLU questions from unrelated subjects (e.g. College Chemistry, Jurisprudence). In-context provision of forgotten facts is untested (per the record, not stated in the paper).
statements.problem: The paper has no list of untested items. The 'untested' line comes from the catalog record. The substance holds: the paper does not supply the forgotten facts in context.

statements.correction: RMU on WMDP best attacks: Zephyr WMDP-Bio 0.146->0.293 (Hindi), Llama WMDP-Bio 0.108->0.213, Zephyr Cyber 0.106->0.241, Llama Cyber 0.060->0.164. The 0.29-0.40 range (originals 0.646-0.710) covers Zephyr RMU Bio set and WMDP-Bio, Llama LLMU Bio set and WMDP-Bio, and Llama RMU Bio set.
statements.problem: Under the 'RMU on WMDP' bullet it gives 0.29-0.40 for this study. That range spans five pairs, including LLMU and the Biology dataset. Only one is RMU on WMDP (r18, 0.293).

statements.correction: Zephyr WMDP RMU (r18, r45) is the WMDP authors' released model. Zephyr Biology RMU, both Llama RMU runs and all LLMU models were trained by the authors (LLMU with LoRA).
statements.problem: 'Self-implemented' RMU is wrong for Zephyr on WMDP, which uses the released Li et al. model. So the checkpoint-dependent training caveat does not apply to r18/r45.
